content:
Let the track length be \(L\), and let the fastest speed be \(V\). The fastest runner finishes at time  
\[
T=\frac{2L}{V}.
\]

For any blue runner with speed \(b\) and red runner with speed \(r\):

- Catch-up meetings would occur at times \(\frac{L}{|b-r|}, \frac{3L}{|b-r|},\dots\).  
  Since \(9<b,r<12\), we have \(|b-r|<3\), so
  \[
  \frac{L}{|b-r|}>\frac{L}{3}>\frac{2L}{9}>T.
  \]
  Thus no catch-up occurs before the fastest finishes.

- Head-on meetings occur at
  \[
  t_k=\frac{(2k+1)L}{b+r},\quad k=0,1,2,\dots
  \]
  Since \(b+r>18\) and \(V<12\), we have \(b+r>1.5V\), so
  \[
  t_1=\frac{3L}{b+r}<\frac{2L}{V}=T.
  \]
  Also \(b+r\le 2V\), so
  \[
  t_2=\frac{5L}{b+r}\ge \frac{5L}{2V}>T.
  \]
  Hence exactly two head-on meetings occur for each blue-red pair.

There are \(5\cdot 5=25\) blue-red pairs, so the total number of checks is
\[
25\cdot 2=50.
\]

\[
\boxed{50}
\]
